title: Localization and scalar-extension descent of Tate-source comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, with $g_{T,\gamma}=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius $\gamma$ [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated and finite type between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with geometric base change smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$. Use $P_fK=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$, the canonical source comparison $b_{f,K}$, and the strict source datum $(Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d)[2d]b_{f,K}$ of [def-pur-tate-datum], with $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. For $\Lambda=E$ the source-comparison, coefficient, Cartesian-pullback and smooth-composition identities over $\mathcal O_E$ (on the realized systems of [lem-pur-tate-source-strict-system-identities]) have equal localized images under rationalization, with the arrow action prescribed by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For every finite extension $E\subseteq L\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, let $R_T$ denote scalar extension, $C_T:R_TG_T\cong G'_TR_T$, $K'=R_YK$, and $a_P:R_XP_fK\cong P'_fK'$ the canonical scalar comparison from [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-fix-operation-reduction]. With $\varphi_{K'}=R_Y(\varphi_K)C_{Y,K}^{-1}$ and $\psi_{f,K}=(Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d)[2d]b_{f,K}$ one has
$$a_PR_X(\psi_{f,K})=\psi'_{f,K'}G'_X(a_P)C_{X,P_fK}.$$
The scalar comparison is the identity for $L=E$ and is compatible with successive finite extensions. Over $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ these arrows and equations define well-defined morphism classes by representing the finitely many input objects, arrows and comparisons at one common finite coefficient field, independently of further extension. Every assertion uses the bounded constructible finite-Tor domains of the named comparisons, with the rational/common-stage categories rather than discrete non-torsion small-etale coefficients. The tensor comparison in $b_{f,K}$ is $\mu$ of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso].

proof.text: Apply the functorial derived inverse limit to the whole-system equations of [lem-pur-tate-source-strict-system-identities], then rationalize. The raw localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] has the same objects and sends an integral arrow $u$ to $u\otimes1$; hence equal integral composites have equal images. More generally [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] preserves comparison equations, composition and whiskering. The explicit arrow action in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] sends $F(u\otimes a)$ to $F(u)\otimes a$ and $(v\otimes a)\otimes^L(w\otimes b)$ to $(v\otimes^Lw)\otimes ab$. Thus the localized comparisons have precisely the prescribed action, including on rational arrows represented by sums of pure tensors. This gives the localized source, coefficient, Cartesian-pullback and smooth-composition identities.

source.place: Source-of-purity composite: rationalized image of the integral datum.

proof.text:
Fix $E\subseteq L$. Write $F=Lf^*$, $F'=Lf_L^*$, $T=E_X(d)$, $T'=L_X(d)$, and $\alpha:R_XF\cong F'R_Y$. Use the normalized pullback scalar comparisons of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], rationalized as in Step 1; in particular $C_T$ is the comparison for $g_T$. That lemma's composition/scalar equation, applied to $fg_X=g_Yf$, identifies the two scalar transports of the commuting-pullback comparison $c_f:G_XF\cong FG_Y$. The tensor comparison $\mu_{g_X}$ commutes with scalar extension by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. The tensor/scalar maps are natural by [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], and use the canonical shifted comparisons of [lem-weil-completed-scalar-chain-shift]. Put $H=(FG_YK\otimes^LG_XT)[2d]$. Define $a_H:R_XH\cong(F'G'_YK'\otimes^LG'_XT')[2d]$ by scalar tensor comparison followed on the first factor by $F'(C_{Y,K})\alpha_{G_YK}$ and on the second by $G'_X(t)C_{X,T}$, where $t:R_XT\cong T'$ is the canonical twist comparison. Expand the defining $b=(c_f\otimes1)[2d]\mu_{g_X}[2d]$ of [def-pur-tate-datum]. Pasting the two component squares just cited, and using functoriality of tensor, gives
$$a_HR_X(b_{f,K})=b'_{f,K'}G'_X(a_P)C_{X,P_fK}.$$
All these are comparisons of actual constructed functors, not independently chosen isomorphisms.

source.place: First arrow of the displayed source composite: pullback, tensor and shift comparisons under coefficient extension.

proof.text:
Let $D=(F\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d)[2d]:H\to P_fK$ and $D'=(F'\varphi_{K'}\otimes\tau'_d)[2d]$. Apply [lem-pur-canonical-tate-arrow-naturality] with scheme $T=X$ and exponent $r=d\ge0$. First take its coefficient functor to be completed integral extension $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_L$, with the specified strict quotient systems; then apply rationalization as in Step 1. The statement explicitly includes these localized images, so for the field scalar functor $R_X$ its equation says
$$tR_X(\tau_d)=\tau'_dG'_X(t)C_{X,T}.$$
Naturality of $\alpha$ in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] gives
$$\alpha_K R_X(F\varphi_K)=F'(R_Y\varphi_K)\alpha_{G_YK}.$$
Substitute $\varphi_{K'}=R_Y(\varphi_K)C_{Y,K}^{-1}$. The first-factor expression in $D'a_H$ becomes $F'(R_Y\varphi_K)\alpha_{G_YK}$, since $F'(C_Y^{-1})F'(C_Y)=1$; the second-factor expression is $tR_X(\tau_d)$ by the displayed Tate equation. Naturality of the scalar tensor comparison and its shift [lem-weil-completed-scalar-chain-shift] now give $a_PR_X(D)=D'a_H$.

source.place: Second arrow of the displayed source composite: datum and canonical Tate arrow.

proof.text:
Since $\psi_{f,K}=Db_{f,K}$ and $\psi'_{f,K'}=D'b'_{f,K'}$, Steps 2 and 3 give
$$a_PR_X(\psi_{f,K})=D'a_HR_X(b_{f,K})=D'b'_{f,K'}G'_X(a_P)C_{X,P_fK}=\psi'_{f,K'}G'_X(a_P)C_{X,P_fK}.$$
Both sides run from $R_XG_XP_fK$ to $P'_fK'$; in particular the rightmost $C_X$ cannot be omitted before identifying these sources.

source.place: Composition of the two displayed source arrows; associativity and substitution.

proof.text: For $E\subseteq L\subseteq M$, the pullback and tensor scalar comparisons satisfy the identity and tower laws of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]; the normalized commuting-pullback comparison has these same laws by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For the twist factor use [lem-weil-integral-twist-scalar-coherence], whose equation compares the successive twist/scalar maps with the direct one. Its identity clause uses the tensor unitor, so the comparison is the identity after the prescribed identity-extension identification. The shift of scalar extension is normalized by the quotient comparison in [lem-weil-completed-scalar-chain-shift]. Its termwise scalar associator multiplies coefficient factors in degree zero, so shifting that associator introduces no additional sign. Composing these factor equations proves the identity and successive-extension laws for $a_P$ and $b$. The Tate-arrow equation in Step 3 is natural for these same comparisons, so the source-datum equation of Step 4 is compatible with them. Rationalization preserves every equation by Step 1.

source.place: Coefficient transport: identity and successive finite field extensions.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]: each object and arrow has a finite coefficient field of definition, and equality of representatives means equality after extension to a further common finite field. There are only finitely many objects, arrows and comparisons in each asserted diagram. Repeated composita therefore give one finite field containing their fields of definition; any finitely many equalities of classes can also be witnessed after one further enlargement. Form $b$, $D$, $\psi$ and the comparisons at that field. By Steps 4 and 5 their further extensions agree through the prescribed comparisons. A different choice of representatives or initial field is compared at a common enlargement, where the equations already hold. Hence the morphism classes and equations are well-defined. The conjugated arrow action is exactly [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]: the intermediate comparison and its inverse cancel when composing. All uses of reduction and coefficient comparison retain the bounded constructible finite-Tor domains of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; at field stages these are $D^b_c$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. No passage to discrete non-torsion small-etale coefficients occurs.
